prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1476; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Police report requested. No apparent airbag deployment reported by either party. Liability appears clear pending scene photos and statements.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. Attorney letter of representation received and logged. All further contact to be directed through counsel only. Claimant reports neck and lower back discomfort; medical treatment in progress. Diagnosis listed as lumbar strain, no fracture indicated in initial records.

Entry 3: Received itemized medical records from claimant's treating provider through counsel. Records document back strain with muscle spasm and prescribed physical therapy. No surgical recommendation at this time. Reviewing treatment timeline against date of loss for consistency.

Entry 4: Spoke with defense counsel's office regarding request for updated wage documentation. Claimant reportedly missed several shifts of work. Requested pay stubs and employer verification form through attorney. Vehicle repair estimate reviewed and approved for the insured's rear bumper and trunk panel.

Entry 5: Follow-up with claimant's attorney on outstanding records. Physical therapy progress notes received, showing improving range of motion. File flagged for supervisor review ahead of settlement evaluation. Next diary set for follow-up with counsel in thirty days.
